strengths: Formalizes a highly practical and realistic problem setting: text-driven amodal 3D generation, which aims to resolve occlusion-induced visual ambiguity in single-image reconstruction by utilizing text prompts.

Provides a strong theoretical foundation. The paper elegantly proves that attention logit smoothing is equivalent to a low-pass filter on the generative velocity field, and successfully derives stability bounds and Wasserstein distance guarantees to justify this relaxation.

The proposed RelaxFlow framework is training-free and plug-and-play, making it widely applicable to state-of-the-art flow-based feedforward 3D generators like TRELLIS and SAM3D without requiring expensive retraining.

Introduces two carefully designed diagnostic benchmarks (ExtremeOcc-3D and AmbiSem-3D) that target extreme occlusion and semantic branching scenarios, which are highly beneficial for future research in this direction.
Demonstrates robust quantitative and qualitative performance improvements across different backbones, backed by a comprehensive user study and thorough ablation studies.
weaknesses: The framework heavily relies on external 2D prior images (retrieved or generated via a text-to-image model). This introduces a pipeline dependency where the quality and consistency of the 3D generation can be bottlenecked by the quality of the 2D image generator.

Although the authors claim the computational overhead is negligible, concatenating visual tokens from $N$ prior images for cross-attention inevitably increases key-value sequence lengths. A quantitative breakdown of the latency and GPU memory overhead under different values of $N$ would strengthen the paper's efficiency claims.

The visibility mask calculation (Eq. 41) relies on the camera pose estimated by the backbone network. Under extreme occlusion, pose estimation itself is often error-prone. The paper would benefit from discussing or evaluating how robust RelaxFlow is to inaccurate pose estimations from the backbone.

strengths: Formulates a novel and highly practical task: text-driven amodal 3D generation, which uses text prompts to resolve occlusion-induced ambiguities while strictly preserving visible details.
Proposes an elegant training-free framework (RelaxFlow) that can be easily plugged into existing state-of-the-art feedforward 3D generators like TRELLIS and SAM3D.

Provides a solid theoretical justification, proving that attention logit smoothing is equivalent to a low-pass filter on the generative vector field, which suppresses high-frequency conflicts and stabilizes the generation process.
Introduces two high-quality diagnostic benchmarks (ExtremeOcc-3D and AmbiSem-3D) to systematically evaluate amodal 3D generation under severe occlusion and semantic branching.
Demonstrates superior qualitative and quantitative performance, backed by a thorough user study showing a strong preference for RelaxFlow.
weaknesses: Relies on an external text-to-image model (e.g., Z-Image) to generate visual proxies from text prompts. This introduces an extra dependency and potential failure modes if the generated 2D priors are of low quality or contain unwanted biases.
Produces unrealistic 'concept fusions' when the input observation and text-derived priors are fundamentally incompatible (as discussed in the failure cases section).
Requires tuning of multiple hyperparameters (e.g., relaxation strength σ, cutoff threshold ρ, and number of priors N) which might vary depending on the base feedforward 3D generator used.

strengths: Formulates an important and highly practical task: text-driven amodal 3D generation, which directly addresses the semantic ambiguity of heavily occluded regions in single-view 3D generation.
The method is training-free and plug-and-play, demonstrating generalizability across recent state-of-the-art feedforward architectures like TRELLIS and SAM3D.
Provides a solid theoretical foundation, proving that logit smoothing acts as a low-pass filter on the generative vector field, which mathematically bounds estimation error and improves stability.
Introduces two new diagnostic benchmarks (ExtremeOcc-3D and AmbiSem-3D) specifically designed to evaluate extreme occlusion and multi-hypothesis semantic completion.
Presents compelling qualitative and quantitative results, backed up by a user study, showing a clear advantage over conventional baseline models.
weaknesses: Relies heavily on external visual priors: Since feedforward models are visual-token conditioned, the system depends on an external text-to-image generator or retrieval pool to create visual proxies. This makes the final quality dependent on the quality of these 2D generation backbones.

Increased memory overhead: Concatenating visual prior tokens ($N=3$ in experiments) increases key-value sequence lengths in cross-attention, which may scale poorly with larger numbers of priors or higher-resolution tokenizers.

Dependency on pose estimation: The visibility-aware fusion mechanism used in the latent refinement stage relies on the accuracy of the estimated object pose from the backbone. Inaccurate pose estimations can lead to misaligned visibility masks and introduce visual artifacts.

Limitations in handling conflicting conditions: As highlighted in the failure cases, when the user-provided prompt and input observation are semantically incompatible, the framework tends to generate distorted interpolations ('concept fusion') instead of resolving the conflict gracefully.

strengths: Formalizes the novel and practical task of text-driven amodal 3D generation, addressing a critical gap in single-view 3D reconstruction under occlusion.

Proposes a training-free, plug-and-play framework (RelaxFlow) that can be seamlessly applied to state-of-the-art feedforward 3D generators (like TRELLIS and SAM3D) without requiring expensive retraining.

Provides a strong theoretical foundation showing that attention-logit smoothing acts as a low-pass filter on the generative vector field, which mathematically reduces semantic estimation error and tightens Wasserstein bounds.
Introduces two well-designed diagnostic benchmarks (ExtremeOcc-3D and AmbiSem-3D) specifically tailored to evaluate amodal completion and semantic branching.
Delivers convincing qualitative and quantitative results, backed by user studies, extensive baseline comparisons, and thorough ablation studies.
weaknesses: Increases inference-time computational overhead (roughly 1.8x to 2.4x slower) due to the evaluation of dual branches during sampling.

Relies on external visual proxies (text-to-image generators or image retrieval systems) to form the Multi-Prior Consensus, introducing dependency on the quality and consistency of these external sources.
Sensitivity to hyperparameters such as the Gaussian blur scale, linear cutoff schedule, and the number of prior images requires careful tuning, as extreme values can degrade generation quality.

strengths: Formalizes a novel and practical task of text-driven amodal 3D generation, providing a principled way to resolve occlusion-induced single-view ambiguity using text prompts.
The proposed RelaxFlow framework is training-free and easily integrated into state-of-the-art feedforward 3D models (such as TRELLIS and SAM3D) as a plug-and-play module.

Provides a solid theoretical formulation showing that attention-logit smoothing behaves as a low-pass filter on the generative vector field, which minimizes semantic estimation error and provides a tighter Wasserstein-2 stability bound.
Introduces two valuable diagnostic benchmarks, ExtremeOcc-3D and AmbiSem-3D, and demonstrates state-of-the-art performance with thorough quantitative, qualitative, and user-study evaluations.
weaknesses: Relies on generating or retrieving intermediate 2D prior images from text prompts (via Z-Image or datasets) because current feedforward models cannot directly ingest text tokens, which introduces an external dependency.
Inference time is significantly increased (by 1.8x to 2.5x) due to the parallel evaluation of dual branches (Observation and Semantic-Prior) at each flow/diffusion step.

The method introduces several heuristic hyperparameters (e.g., linear cutoff threshold ρ, smoothing strength σ, and visibility mask parameters) which may require manual tuning across different backbones.

strengths: Novel and highly practical task formulation of text-driven amodal 3D generation, providing explicit linguistic control to resolve visual ambiguities under occlusion instead of relying on dataset-driven single completions.

Strong theoretical justification that connects attention-logit blurring to a low-pass filter on the generative vector field, proving it reduces semantic estimation error and provides Wasserstein stability bounds.

Innovative multi-prior consensus strategy that allows training-free alignment with visual-token-conditioned 3D generators by feeding multiple generated/retrieved priors into cross-attention in a single pass.
Thorough evaluation on two newly introduced diagnostic benchmarks (ExtremeOcc-3D and AmbiSem-3D), with extensive comparisons against diverse baseline families and a user study.
Compelling qualitative results showing successful preservation of observed high-frequency details while steering the unobserved geometry to match the intent prompt.
weaknesses: High dependence on external text-to-image generators or retrieval systems to obtain high-quality visual priors; failures in these prior models can propagate to the 3D generation.
Significant computational overhead introduced by the dual-branch sampling, which increases inference time by 1.82x to 2.46x depending on the backbone.

The spatial visibility-aware fusion relies on camera pose estimation; when applied to backbones without pose estimation (like TRELLIS), this component must be disabled, leading to a drop in performance.
Sensitivity to multiple hyperparameters (such as $\sigma$, $\rho$, and $N$), which may require careful manual tuning when adapted to different 3D generation backbones.
